svg.title: The axis swap from Blender into FLVER space
svg.desc: Top, animated over 30 seconds: fixed axes drawn as Blender's Front view shows them, X to the right, Z up and Y into the scene. A character stands facing the viewer, up +Z, forward -Y, left side +X. Its coordinates are rotated -90 degrees about X, which lays it on its back, up +Y and forward +Z; then Z is negated, a reflection, which turns it face down, forward -Z, with the left side still at +X. Below, three panels show the character's axes seen from in front, with its left side to the right of the screen. In Blender, X points right, Z up and Y into the screen: right-handed, with forward along -Y. After the rotation, Y points up and Z out of the screen: still right-handed, with forward along +Z. After Z is negated, Z points into the screen: left-handed, as in FLVER, with forward along -Z and the left side still along +X.

g.text: Each panel: the character seen from in front.
